clue.text: Hard to move, dismissing first argument

indicators.note: dismissing first tells us to drop the opening letter of the word for hard to move

parts.note: something stiff is rigid and hard to move

explanation.surface: A rigid object refuses to budge, and the first dispute is thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a minor quarrel, so it is a mild synonym for an argument.

clue.text: Delay in Spooner's security fix?

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: bail is money given as security
to tack is to fix or fasten

explanation.surface: A delay in fixing a security problem, credited to the famously muddled Reverend Spooner.
explanation.definitionFit: A queue of traffic held up on a road is a form of delay.

clue.text: Film buff cheers one in it

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or fan
ta is British informal for thanks, as is cheers

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: it, meaning sex appeal, is SA in crosswords
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A movie enthusiast cheers for somebody appearing in the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasia is the 1940 Disney animated movie set to classical music.

clue.text: Give excellent review to book, then catch opening of this film

parts.note: to rave about something is to praise it wildly
to catch what someone says is to hear it

indicators.note: opening of points to the first letter of the word this

explanation.surface: A critic praises a book highly, then catches the start of this film.
explanation.walkthrough: The book's abbreviation B comes first in the answer although the clue mentions it after the review.
explanation.definitionFit: Braveheart is the 1995 Mel Gibson movie about William Wallace, an example of a film.

clue.text: It supplies a little colour in set

definitions.text: It supplies a little colour in set

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hair product adds a hint of colour to a freshly set hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes a hair rinse, which tints hair that has been set.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun stands for the thing described: a rinse is a tint applied to the hair.

clue.text: Some particular bet reviewed, raised? That's showing backbone

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, means the letters read upwards, so backwards
some says only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A particular wager is reconsidered and raised, which shows some nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: The run LARBETREV sits in 'particular bet reviewed' and 'raised' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertebral means relating to the vertebrae, the bones that make up the spine.

clue.text: Musical arrangement for eighty choirs that's not right

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reorders the letters of the following words
that's not says a letter is left out of the fodder

explanation.surface: A musical score is arranged for eighty choirs, which seems wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not right' removes R from EIGHTYCHOIRS before 'arrangement for' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: High Society is the 1956 film musical with Bing Crosby and Grace Kelly, later staged.

clue.text: Writer finally brought in article on historic English composer

indicators.note: brought in means put inside another piece

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of Writer

parts.note: historic means old

explanation.surface: An author's last piece is added to an old article about a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Malcolm Arnold was a twentieth-century English composer of symphonies and film scores.

clue.text: Gift? Expression of gratitude supplied

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
lent means supplied on loan

explanation.surface: A present arrives, and thanks are offered for what was given.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural aptitude, often called a gift.

clue.text: Legal groups covering both ends of the country?

parts.note: in, as in dressed in a coat, means covered by or wearing
the far ends of a country, north and south, are N and S

explanation.surface: Lawyers' associations seem to spread from one end of the land to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both ends of the country' is not C and Y here but its geographic extremes, north and south. The Inns of Court are London's four barristers' societies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inns of Court are the professional associations every English barrister must belong to, so they are legal bodies.

clue.text: You'll have seen this sort of clue before

definitions.text: You'll have seen this sort of clue before

parts.words: You'll have seen this sort of clue before
parts.note: a clue met before is derivative, lacking any novelty, and the clue itself describes such a thing

explanation.surface: The setter wryly admits a clue is a repeat of something you have met before.
explanation.definitionFit: Something already seen elsewhere is derivative and lacks novelty, which is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Girl's poise snaring hearts, though not first of Americans

indicators.note: snaring means catching another piece inside
though not says a letter is taken away from the word for poise

parts.note: poise is balance or composure

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of Americans

parts.note: H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A young woman's composure catches hearts, though not among Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A (the first of Americans) from BALANCE to get BLANCE, then 'snaring' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Blanche is a female first name, so it fits the definition of a girl.

clue.text: Spoils children in relaxed training centre

indicators.note: in places the other pieces within this one

parts.note: cool can mean calm and relaxed
to spoil is to harm

explanation.surface: Someone spoils the children at an easy-going place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A school that teaches etiquette and poise to young women is a kind of training establishment.

clue.text: Greek character's no problem speaking English? Just the reverse

indicators.note: just the reverse tells us to read the assembled letters backwards

parts.note: someone with no speech problem has no lisp

explanation.surface: A Greek person claims to have no trouble speaking English, or perhaps the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the reverse' seems to undo the claim; instead it turns NOLISPE round.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is a character in that script.

clue.text: Critical atmosphere almost splendid after chapter's accepted

indicators.note: after places the trimmed splendid word behind the chapter-filled atmosphere word
accepted means taken in, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: the climate of a place or time is its prevailing atmosphere or mood
C is the abbreviation for chapter

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the word for splendid is dropped

parts.note: rich can mean splendid or sumptuous

explanation.surface: A tense mood that is nearly glorious follows once a chapter is approved.
explanation.walkthrough: Chapter's C goes into the atmosphere word, and the trimmed splendid word comes after; 'after' orders the pieces rather than linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A climacteric point is a turning point or crucial stage, so the word means decisive or crucial.

clue.text: Duke, in defeat, elevated and elevated symbol of reconciliation?

indicators.note: in means put inside the other piece
elevated, in a down clue, means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat
rose means went up or was raised

explanation.surface: A duke, beaten in battle, is raised up and honoured as a sign of peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated' first turns ROUT into TUOR and D goes in; the second 'elevated' is a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor rose combined the red rose of Lancaster and white rose of York after the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Year's wrangling to block reduction of large disputed field

indicators.note: to block means sit inside another piece
reduction of means trimming the last letter

parts.note: great means large

indicators.note: wrangling suggests the letters argue and change places

parts.note: the word Year is taken as written

explanation.surface: A year of arguments blocks a reduction of a large contested area of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrangling' makes YARE from YEAR; 'reduction of' cuts GREAT to GREA.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter that is unclear, where right and wrong are debated, is figuratively an ambiguous zone.

clue.text: Mystery individual following Western carrier

indicators.note: following puts this piece after the others

parts.note: a hod is a builder's carrier for bricks
a unit is a single individual thing

explanation.surface: A mysterious person follows a Western courier.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective story in which the culprit is revealed at the end is a type of mystery novel.

clue.text: Heart that's subsequently broken in fantasy land?

parts.note: the heart of something is its middle

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters of the word referred to are rearranged, placed after the first part

parts.note: that refers back to the word Heart in the clue

explanation.surface: A broken heart is described as a fantasy, as if love's realm were imaginary.
explanation.walkthrough: The word Heart works twice: once as a synonym, then as letters rearranged into EARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-earth is the invented world of Tolkien's Lord of the Rings, a classic fantasy realm.

clue.text: Illegible lettering: that is, crude line

parts.note: sc, for scilicet, means that is or namely
raw means crude or unrefined

explanation.surface: Handwriting that cannot be read, namely a rough line.
explanation.definitionFit: Messy handwriting that is hard to read is called a scribble or scrawl.

clue.text: British cooking, cold, very cold

parts.note: a balti is a style of curry developed in Birmingham

explanation.surface: British food is served chilly, very chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: A BALTI is a curry style that originated in Birmingham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltic is informal British slang for freezing weather, from the chilly Baltic Sea.

clue.text: Court dismissing unknown opportunist

indicators.note: dismissing means the letter for an unknown is sent away

parts.note: Chancery is a division of the English High Court
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A judge throws out an obscure chancer who tries his luck in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancer is someone who takes risks for gain, a British informal word for an opportunist.

clue.text: Not showing usual colour after swallowing whiskey, but not weepy

indicators.note: swallowing means one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: dyed hair or cloth no longer shows its natural colour
rye is a type of whiskey

explanation.surface: Someone looks pale after a whiskey, but is not tearful.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without tears, even in sad circumstances, is the sense of the hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Fool our team into lifting mattress

indicators.note: into puts one piece inside the other
lifting, in a down clue, means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a bed is a mattress
we means our team or us

explanation.surface: Someone tricks our team into hoisting a mattress.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweeb is a boring, socially inept person, a slang word for a fool or nerd.

clue.text: More struggling after a firm dismisses good scientist

indicators.note: after puts the jumbled piece behind the earlier pieces
dismisses says a letter is removed from the word for firm

parts.note: strong can mean firm or solid

indicators.note: struggling indicates the letters of More are jumbled

explanation.surface: Further struggles follow when a company sacks a decent researcher.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomer studies stars and planets, a kind of scientist.

clue.text: River enclosed by revolutionary modern architect

indicators.note: enclosed by means placed within the other piece
revolutionary means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: modern means new

explanation.surface: A river runs through the work of a radical modern designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral, the archetypal English architect.

clue.text: Clash of rivals left boy swimming round river

indicators.note: round means wrapped around another piece
swimming suggests the letters of boy move about

parts.note: the Calder is a river in West Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A lad goes swimming around a river while being left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The Calder is a Yorkshire river. A local derby is a match between neighbouring rival teams, as in British football.
explanation.definitionFit: A derby between two teams from the same area is a contest between natural rivals.

clue.text: Shops closing early: time for drink

indicators.note: closing early means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a mall is a set of shops

explanation.surface: When the shops shut early, it's time for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt whisky is a common drink, and malt alone is used for it.
